pairs.why: A hangs flat on a striped wall with a soft cast shadow and a matte rim, like the real wall clock; B stands on a floor and its rim is glossier and more toy-like.
B is a chunky close-up navy fixture with three large glowing lenses, like the real card; A is a small, distant spotlight on a thin chrome truss.
The two are nearly identical; A's dome and ground read slightly cleaner, and B has a bit more speckle and glass glare.
B is built like a real calculator with numbered keys and cyan operator keys, like the real card; A's blank keys look like an unfinished prop.
A has smoother surfaces and the lower panel structure of the real door; B adds stucco and wood-grain texture, which the lessons show is too texture-y.
Both are close; A's chrome-ringed eyepieces and simpler blue frame are marginally nearer the real viewer, and B's lenses are a bit glossier.
B's round anchor badge and three-quarter view match the real cap; A's shield badge departs from the real design.
A's segmented, carved-wood trunk and matte leaves match the real palm; B's trunk is smoother and glossier, like a plastic toy.
